correctness.rationale: The cell Bernoulli variance is computed locally. The curvature term in each n-cell is u²/n, and only O(1) boundary cells per column have nonzero variance, so replacing the curve by its tangent changes the variance sum by O(1). The resulting phase dependence is v_{2i/n}({i²/n}). Complete quadratic Gauss-sum bound |G_n(k,l)|²<=n gcd(2k,n) proves equidistribution for all positive integer n, not only primes. Averaging unit vertical phase gives K(s)=.5 E|s(U1-U2)-(V1-V2)| with two exact rational branches; integrating K(2x) gives target 311/1440+log(2)/24. Independent code directly integrates actual curved boundary cells at grids up to n=4000 and exactly checks the phase-average integral; convergence tests are corroborative only.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns fixed parabola and all integer grid sizes only, not generic smooth curves.
Finite calculations are not the Weyl equidistribution proof.
